paragraphs: The University of New Haven is a private research university located in West Haven, Connecticut, founded in 1920 as New Haven Junior College — originally a division of Northeastern University. Today the university enrolls roughly 9,200 students across more than 100 undergraduate programs and over 110 graduate programs, organized into five colleges and schools.

The university is internationally recognized for forensic science and criminal justice education through the Henry C. Lee College of Criminal Justice and Forensic Sciences and the Henry C. Lee Institute of Forensic Science, which opened on campus in 1998. The institute features crime-scene laboratories, classrooms, and a 104-seat lecture hall named after the world-renowned forensic scientist Dr. Henry C. Lee.

Other strong areas include the Tagliatela College of Engineering (established 1920), Pompea College of Business, the College of Arts and Sciences with programs in marine biology, environmental science, communication, and game design, and the School of Health Sciences. The university holds accreditation from the New England Commission of Higher Education since 1948.

The University of New Haven attracts a diverse international cohort drawn by hands-on programs, professional placements, and proximity to New Haven and New York City. In 2026, U.S. News & World Report ranked the university No. 76 among Regional Universities North.

Также сильны Tagliatela College of Engineering (с 1920), Pompea College of Business, College of Arts and Sciences (marine biology, environmental science, communication, game design) и School of Health Sciences. С 1948 года университет аккредитован New England Commission of Higher Education.
